Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

K-9 Officer Rico was stabbed in the neck by 46-year-old Jose Pascacio, suffering severe injuries to multiple veins, arteries, and his trachea. Pascaccio was shot and killed by officers at the scene. Rico was rushed to the Southwest Animal Emergency Clinic, where surgeons were able to stop the bleeding. Officer Eric DeMille, Rico's handler, was told his partner might need to have his leg amputated. But less than three weeks later, Rico made a full recovery and was back on the job. A blood transfusion from another K-9 officer named Enzo helped stabilize Rico and the community quickly rallied behind them. As Officer DeMille explained, the support that we have received from the community has been like nothing I have ever seen. RICO has received treats, bones, stuffed animals, toys, blankets, and more. DeMille went on to say, I am so thankful for Rico's speedy recovery and that I don't have to work without him. Him being with me gives me and my family more comfort. He is loved by the whole family. RICO was later awarded the Medal of Valor, the department's highest honor, alongside Officer DeMille and Officer Jordan Bogan. Hurricane City Police stated the medal is awarded to officers who distinguish themselves by conspicuous bravery and heroism above and beyond the normal demands of police service, adding that recipients have performed an act displaying extreme courage while consciously facing imminent peril.

alleged_crimes.label: Assault on a police officer (stabbing K-9)

event_summary.short: Hurricane City Police responded to a man acting strangely at a gas station on December 26, 2002. After a brief pursuit, the suspect caused a multi-vehicle crash, then broke into a nearby apartment. When officers entered, the suspect stabbed police K-9 Rico in the neck. Officers shot and killed the suspect.
